# Singularity design system
<!-- GENERATED by scripts/system/build.ts (npm run system). Do not edit. -->

Pick a part from this list before writing a class or a value. A part that fits is used as it is; none fits means ask the owner. Never invent a control class.
Detail of one: `npm run ds -- part <id>`. Search by need: `npm run ds -- find "<what you need>"`. Tokens: `npm run ds -- token <words>`. Everything: tokens/system.json.

## Parts
`id` classes: what it is. Use: when. Not: situation → part to use instead.
- `button-filled` .button-filled: The accent fill under its own words; the most prominent button. Use: It is the one action that commits a sheet, a dialog or an empty page: Save, Add category, Listen now; It saves or submits a form sheet, or confirms a dialog. Not: Another filled button is on the same surface: make the second one Tonal → button-tonal.
- `button-tonal` .button-tonal: The accent container under its own words, with no outline; quieter than Filled. Use: It is the alternative beside a Filled button; It is a labelled add or reorder action on a list: Add source, Add section, Reorder. Not: It is the only action that commits the surface → button-filled.
- `button-text` .button-text: An accent label with no container until it is hovered or pressed; the quietest button. Use: It dismisses, backs out or repeats: Cancel, Clear, Try again, Hide this; It sits beside a Filled button as the lesser choice. Not: The action must be found at a glance on its own → button-filled.
- `button-danger` .button-danger: A Text button in the danger colour. Use: It is the confirm of a delete, in a dialog that asks first: Delete, Delete source. Not: The action is not destructive, or nobody has been asked to confirm → button-text.
- `switch` .switch-input: A track and a thumb for one setting that is on or off, with its label beside it. Use: A setting is on or off and applies as soon as it is flipped: Sounds, Autoplay, a podcast's Enabled; It sits at the end of a settings row, with the row's label as its name. Not: The choice is one of several values, or needs a Save to apply → filter-chip.
- `slider` .slider-input: A track with a thumb: a value between two ends, set by dragging or by the arrow keys. Use: The value is on a scale where nearby values are alike: Volume, Playback speed, a topic's weight; A person may want to set it without a number in front of them. Not: There are two to five named options and none is between the others → filter-chip.
- `field` .field-input: An outlined box for text a person types: one line, or several lines (multiline). Use: A person types a short value or a few lines: a title, a feed address, a prompt; It sits under its own label in a form or a settings row, and a refused value shows as an invalid field. Not: The value is one of two to four short options → filter-chip.
- `select` .select-outlined .select-tonal: A native select with its own chevron: a person picks one value from a list that is too long to show. Use: A person picks one value from a list of five or more, or of names that are too long for a row of chips; It sits under its own label in a form, or in a toolbar as a sort or a filter. Not: the value is one of two to four short options → segmented-choice.
- `menu` .menu-list .menu-sheet: A short list of actions that opens from an icon button: a row each, with its glyph at the start. Use: A card, a header or a row has more actions than it has room for: Download, Add to queue, Share, Delete; Each action is one tap and needs no choice of its own. Not: The person picks one value from a list → select.
- `banner` .banner-notice .banner-text: A tinted block with an icon, a title, an optional line and at most one text button. Use: A state a person must know about stays on screen: offline, a failed run, a playback error. Not: a message that clears itself → toast.
- `dialog` .dialog-panel .dialog-body: A small centred box with a heading and a row of buttons: one question, one tap. Use: A person confirms what cannot be undone: Delete, Discard, Switch profile. Not: a form that slides in, with fields → sheet.
- `btn-action-tonal` .btn-action-tonal: The one creating action in the side column (Catch up), on the action tone. Use: the Catch up action in the side column. Not: any other button → button-tonal.
- `icon-btn` .icon-btn .press: A glyph in a round 44px target, quiet until used. Use: close a sheet or dialog; a row's more menu (the dots). Not: an action that needs a word → button-text.
- `icon-btn-tonal` .icon-btn-tonal: The secondary icon button: an icon button on the container fill, a circle. Use: the companion of a primary action when it needs only a glyph, such as Share beside Play. Not: a quiet toolbar glyph → icon-btn.
- `play-chip` .chip: The tonal pill that plays a briefing or one story, with its state. Use: play an episode or a story and show idle, current, played, error or preparing; episode duration with a play mark. Not: a choice the user ticks → filter-chip.
- `filter-chip` .filter-chip .filter-chips: A checkbox drawn as a pill; ticked it takes the accent container. Use: tick several topics or categories to include; filter a list by one or more kinds. Not: exactly one of a few values → segmented-choice.
- `segmented-choice` .segmented-choice .segmented-choice-item: One pill of radio items: pick exactly one value. Use: choose one of a few discrete values, such as 3, 5 or 10 minutes; a setting with two to four options. Not: switching between views or tabs → segmented-nav.
- `segmented-nav` .segmented-nav .segmented-nav-tab: A tonal track with one sliding pill: switch between views of the same content. Use: switch between Stories and Transcript; switch the view of one page without leaving it. Not: choosing a value of a setting → segmented-choice.
- `tabs` .tabs-bar .tab: A sticky strip of links to the sections of one page. Use: jump to the sections of a briefing or an episode; tabs inside a card. Not: switching between two views → segmented-nav.
- `row-action` .row-action .settings-text: A row that is one link or button: the whole row responds as a rounded tile. Use: a settings row that opens a sub-page; a menu or list row that navigates. Not: a row that holds a switch or a select → settings-row.
- `card-group` .card-group .rows: A group of rows in one rounded container on the container tone. Use: group several settings rows; a card of chips. Not: a single stat or number → stat-tiles.
- `settings-row` .settings-row .settings-label: A row with a label and an in-place control: a switch, a select or a value. Use: a setting with a switch; a setting with a select. Not: a row that opens another page → row-action.
- `toast` .toast .toast-action: One quiet message at a time on the inverse surface, with an optional action. Use: a brief message with an Undo after a delete; a failure that clears itself. Not: a notice that must stay → banner.
- `empty-state` .empty .empty-actions: A spot illustration, a title, one line and at most two actions, for a page with nothing in it. Use: a page or section with nothing to list yet; no results, offline, not found. Not: a list that has items → card-group.
- `sheet` .sheet-head .sheet-actions: A modal bottom sheet on a phone, a centered dialog from 40rem. Use: a new bottom sheet with a title and a close control; a form in a sheet. Not: a menu of choices → menu.
- `multiselect` .multiselect-trigger: A field-like trigger that opens a list of checkable choices. Use: choose several from a long list; pick sources or topics in a field. Not: a few choices that fit on screen → filter-chip.
- `search-field` .search-field .search-clear: The Library's rounded search pill, on the container tone. Use: search or filter a list by text. Not: a text field in a form → field.
- `source-link` .source-link: The one link out of a story: the publisher's name and an opens-elsewhere mark. Use: link out to a publisher from a story or highlight. Not: a link inside a line of small text → text-link.
- `text-link` .text-link: A link inside a line of small text; the words stay inline, the target is 44px. Use: a link inside a hint or a sentence. Not: a standalone action → button-text.
- `stat-tiles` .stat-tiles: A tile per figure: the value large over its word in muted ink. Use: figures on a dashboard; costs and spend totals. Not: a list of rows → card-group.
- `section-head` .section-head: A section header with more room above than below, so it belongs to what follows. Use: title a group of rows or cards on a page.
- `meta` .meta: One quiet line of facts, separated by centered dots. Use: date, duration and source under a title.
- `cover` .cover: A generated cover image, drawn once per theme. Use: show an episode or briefing cover.
- `fab` .create-fab .add-fab: Floating triggers above the bottom bar: create, add, play. Use: the page's one creating action on a phone; play a story from its cover. Not: an action in a form → button-filled.

## Color roles
Components read only these (never a hex, never a primitive color).
- --color-surface: Page background.
- --color-surface-sunken: Wells, inputs, hover fills, track backgrounds.
- --color-surface-container: The tonal fill of a control that sits on the page: the search pill, a play chip, a second…
- --color-surface-raised: Sheets and dialogs.
- --color-surface-overlay: Floating chrome: mini player, popovers.
- --color-surface-inverse: Toasts.
- --color-on-surface
- --color-on-surface-reading: Running text read under a heading in on-surface: a story's summary, an episode highlight.
- --color-on-surface-muted: Secondary text.
- --color-on-surface-subtle: Tertiary text.
- --color-on-surface-disabled: Disabled controls only.
- --color-on-surface-inverse
- --color-border-hairline: Decorative dividers.
- --color-border-control: Boundary of an input or segmented control.
- --color-track: Rail and scrubber track.
- --color-track-strong: Unplayed item ticks and upcoming nodes.
- --color-accent: Lingonberry.
- --color-accent-hover
- --color-accent-pressed
- --color-accent-subtle: Tint behind the current row.
- --color-accent-container: The selected state of a control: a chosen chip or segment, the current destination, a ton…
- --color-on-accent-container: Text and icons on accent-container.
- --color-accent-container-high: The tone of an action that is not a place: the New episode buttons.
- --color-on-accent-container-high: Text and icons on accent-container-high.
- --color-accent-action: The tone of the one creating action in the side column (Catch up).
- --color-on-accent-action: Text and icons on accent-action, at 4.5:1 in rest, hover and press.
- --color-accent-action-state: The ink accent-action's hover and press layers mix in.
- --color-on-accent
- --color-cover-accent: Defaults to the accent.
- --color-on-cover-accent
- --color-focus-ring
- --color-focus-gap: Inner ring color.
- --color-scrim
- --color-image-outline: 1px outline on covers for perceived edge, per DESIGN.md.
- --color-success
- --color-success-subtle
- --color-warning
- --color-warning-subtle
- --color-danger
- --color-danger-subtle
- --color-info
- --color-info-subtle

## Component tokens
Sizes and bindings per part: cover (10), rail (12), item (4), cta (6), action (4), button (4), mini (8), player (5), control (6), scrubber (10), segmented (5), field (9), switch (7), sheet (6), toast (6), banner (2), archive (2), chip (12), app (1), nav (8), tabs (3), row (3), slider (1), card (6). List one with `npm run ds -- token <group>`.

## Bespoke controls
21 controls are built for one place (the player transport and dock, speed controls, source rows). They are not for reuse. 9 more belong to a part above and are used through it. `npm run ds -- part bespoke` lists all with the reason.
